title: Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips
statement:
You are given a binary array `nums` (every entry is `0` or `1`) and an integer `k`. In one move you pick any block of exactly `k` adjacent positions and invert all of them together: each `0` in the block turns into `1` and each `1` turns into `0`.

Return the smallest number of moves after which every entry of `nums` equals `1`. If no sequence of moves can achieve that, return `-1`.
notes:
## Intuition

Look at the leftmost position. Only one window can still change it without touching anything further left: the window that starts there. So if that entry is currently `0`, the window starting at it must be flipped, and if it is `1`, flipping it would be pointless (each window is used at most once, since flipping twice cancels). Sweeping left to right, every decision is forced, which makes the greedy count the minimum. Trying every subset of windows also works but costs O(2ⁿ).

Physically inverting `k` entries per flip is O(n·k). Instead, track how many flips cover the current index and only record where each flip stops, like a difference array.

## Approach

1. Make `diff` of length `n + 1`; `diff[j]` adjusts the number of covering flips when the sweep reaches `j`.
2. At each index `i`, add `diff[i]` to `active`, the count of flips covering `i`.
3. The current value is `nums[i]` inverted `active` times, so it is `0` exactly when `nums[i] + active` is even.
4. If it is `0` and a window starting at `i` would run past the end, return `-1`.
5. Otherwise flip: increase `flips` and `active`, and decrease `diff[i + k]` so the flip stops covering at `i + k`.
6. Return `flips`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [0, 1, 0]`, `k = 1`. At `i = 0`: `active = 0`, `0 + 0` is even, so flip; `flips = 1`, `active = 1`, `diff[1] = -1`. At `i = 1`: `active` drops back to `0`; `1 + 0` is odd, so leave it. At `i = 2`: `active = 0`, `0 + 0` is even and `2 + 1 <= 3`, so flip; `flips = 2`. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per index.
- Space: O(n) for `diff` (it can be reduced to O(1) by marking `nums` in place).

## Pitfalls

- Flipping all `k` entries for each move is O(n·k), too slow when both are large.
- The window must fit: a `0` at index `i` with `i + k > n` means the answer is `-1`.
- Parity, not the raw count, decides the current value: two flips cancel out.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `diff` | where the count of covering flips changes |
| `active` | number of flips covering the current index |
| `flips` | moves made so far |
| `i` | current index of the sweep |

narration.3: diff[j] records how the number of covering flips changes when the sweep reaches index j.
narration.4: active counts the flips whose windows cover the current index.
narration.7: Sweep the array from left to right; each index is decided exactly once.
narration.8: Apply any change recorded for this index, such as a flip whose window just ended.
narration.9: The entry is currently 0 when its original value plus the covering flips is even.
narration.10: A window starting here would run past the end of the array...
narration.11: ...so this 0 can never be fixed and the task is impossible.
narration.13: Flip the window that starts at i; it is the only one left that can fix this entry.
narration.14: The new flip covers the current index too.
narration.15: Mark index i + k as the place where this flip stops covering.
narration.18: Every entry is now 1; return the number of flips used.
